planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. Supplier's published figure, preserved as stated in the product name: 33 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2). That is 3 m2 over the limit BEFORE any other shed, garage or garden structure already in the garden is counted, and the 30 m2 is a combined total. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record notes the supplier does not state whether 33 m2 is internal or external; if it is internal the external footprint is larger still, so the overrun can only widen, never close. Nothing estimated. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS THE CLASS 3 GARDEN-STRUCTURE ROUTE IS UNAVAILABLE: the area exceeds 30 m2, AND a one-bedroom flat is habitable accommodation, which the Class 3 exemption excludes at any size. THE ROUTE THAT MAY APPLY INSTEAD: the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption introduced by the 2026 Regulations covers 32-45 m2, and 33 m2 sits inside that band. It requires siting to the rear, services linked to the main house, 14 days' written notice to the planning authority, and Building and Fire Regulations compliance, and the provision expires on 31 December 2030. Whether this product qualifies has NOT been determined and cannot be from published information. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this cannot be treated as a normal exempt garden room. Speak to your local authority planning office about the Class 3A notice route, and obtain from Granny Flats Dublin in writing whether 33 m2 is internal or external, the heights, and how water, drainage and electrical services connect to the house.

EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. Supplier's published figure, preserved: 45 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) — 15 m2 over. Class 3 is unavailable twice over: on area, and because a one or two bedroom flat is habitable accommodation, which Class 3 excludes at any size. THE CLASS 3A ROUTE IS AVAILABLE ONLY AT ITS ABSOLUTE OUTER EDGE, AND THE MEASUREMENT BASIS DECIDES IT. The Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption runs from 32 m2 to 45 m2, so 45 m2 sits EXACTLY on the ceiling with zero headroom. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record states the supplier does not say whether 45 m2 is internal or external. If it is EXTERNAL the product just reaches the top of the band. If it is INTERNAL — and for a serviced dwelling with insulated walls the external footprint is materially larger — the true figure exceeds 45 m2 and Class 3A fails too, leaving no exempt route at all. Nothing estimated; no wall thickness added or deducted. Class 3A also requires siting to the rear, services linked to the principal house, at least 14 days' written notice to the planning authority, and Building and Fire Regulations compliance, and the provision expires 31 December 2030. CATALOGUE ISSUE: the product name spans '1 or 2 Bed' at a single 45 m2 figure, so a homeowner cannot tell whether both configurations share that footprint; the variant question is unresolved in the supplier's own material and no reading has been assumed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the product in the range where one unanswered question — internal or external — is the difference between a 14-day notice and a full planning application. Get it in writing before anything else.

EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. Supplier's published figure, preserved: 48 m2. That is 18 m2 over the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) and it ALSO exceeds the upper bound of the 32-45 m2 Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling band, so NEITHER exempt route is available on area alone. As a two-bedroom flat it is habitable accommodation and is excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure route at any size in any event. Full planning permission is indicated. Nothing estimated; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record notes the internal-versus-external basis is unstated, which cannot help here because the figure already exceeds every threshold. CROSS-LAYER INTEGRITY ISSUE recorded once, without altering certified data: the certified AM-004 Insulation record for this product states that 48 m2 exceeds a 40 m2 threshold. That 40 m2 figure is the HOUSE-EXTENSION allowance, which was itself raised to 45 m2 by the 2026 Regulations and does not apply to a detached garden structure. The conclusion in that record — that planning permission is likely to be required — remains correct; only the threshold cited is superseded. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: assume a full planning application. Engage your local authority planning office and a designer before committing to a purchase, and treat any supplier suggestion that this is exempt with caution. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Granny Flats Dublin for the Planning Considerations layer — 4 Garden Room products spanning 25, 33, 45 and 48 m2, all with a published m2 figure of UNSTATED basis. The pattern across the four is the more important finding: EVERY one is habitable accommodation, so not one of them can use the Class 3 garden-structure exemption regardless of area, and the range straddles every statutory threshold Atlas holds — 25 m2 falls below the Class 3A minimum, 33 and 45 m2 sit inside the Class 3A band, and 48 m2 exceeds every route. This also makes the Garden Rooms category placement itself questionable; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Auroom publishes no internal floor area and no footprint for the Aurea; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. As a garden structure a sauna cabin counts toward that combined allowance in full. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint and overall height in writing before ordering, and count the sauna toward your 30 m2 total. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Auroom Wellness for the Planning Considerations layer — 2 Garden Room products, both classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, neither publishing an area, a dimension or a height. CATEGORY ISSUE recorded once: both are wellness and sauna cabins held under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct Product Category, and they should not be compared like-for-like against work-use garden rooms; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. THE PLANNING POINT WORTH CARRYING FORWARD FROM THIS SUPPLIER AND THE OTHER WELLNESS RANGES IN THIS LAYER: sauna cabins, hot-tub enclosures and similar wellness buildings are treated by buyers as equipment and by the Regulations as structures. Their footprints count toward the same 30 m2 as a garden office, and because none of these suppliers publishes a footprint, a homeowner cannot even total their own garden without asking. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Auroom publishes no internal floor area and no footprint for the Quu; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and no wall thickness subtracted. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2) therefore cannot be tested. THE POINT THE CERTIFIED RECORD MAKES AND WHICH BUYERS ROUTINELY MISS: an outdoor sauna cabin IS a garden structure for Class 3 purposes and counts toward the combined 30 m2 alongside any shed, garage or garden room already on the plot — so its area matters even though the building is small. A sauna bought as a wellness purchase rather than a building purchase is exactly the kind of structure that quietly consumes the allowance a homeowner was saving for a garden office. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. CATEGORY ISSUE: Auroom supplies wellness and sauna cabins held under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct Product Category; they should not be compared like-for-like against work-use garden rooms. Recorded, not corrected. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint and overall height in writing, and add the sauna to your running total of back-garden structures before planning anything else.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Ballyfree Garden Sheds publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no derivable footprint for this record; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2) therefore cannot be tested. The record name identifies a product type rather than a model, so there is no size-bearing designation to work from either. Conditions applying regardless of area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. SUPPLIER OMISSION: neither a footprint nor a height is published, so neither statutory test can be run. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint in metres, the measurement basis and the roof height and covering from Ballyfree in writing before ordering, then add the footprint to every other structure already in the back garden and check the combined total against 30 m2. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Ballyfree Garden Sheds for the Planning Considerations layer — 1 Garden Room product, classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA with no published area, dimension or height. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Berko is Northern Ireland based (Dungiven, Co. Derry), where the Irish regime does not apply. For a Republic site: 30 m2 back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), combined across structures, behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Atlas holds no verified floor area. Homeowner implication: confirm floor area and applicable jurisdiction before assuming exemption. SUPPLIER STATUS — BERKO POD SYSTEMS, 3 Garden Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 3 — The Beehive, The Shepherds Hut and The Luxury Lodge — hold the verification classification; none carries a verified floor area and nothing has been estimated. TWO SEPARATE OBSTACLES SIT IN FRONT OF THIS RANGE, and neither is about size. FIRST, JURISDICTION: Berko operates from Northern Ireland, where the Irish exempted-development regime does not apply at all, so the 30 m2 figures above govern only a Republic of Ireland site and any planning guidance the supplier gives from its own jurisdiction must not be read across. SECOND, USE: a Lodge and a Shepherd's Hut are both marketed for overnight occupation, and habitable use falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption at any floor area, so for those two products the use condition decides the outcome before any measurement does; the Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) may be the applicable route instead but cannot be tested without an area. VOCABULARY LIMITATION recorded once: the approved classification set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use. BOUNDARY NOTE: Berko also holds a fourth product, The Treehouse, in the Treehouses category, outside the Garden Room certification boundary; it carries a Planning value and is counted separately. Recorded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit Repair.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND NOTE THE JURISDICTION. Berko is based in Dungiven, Co. Derry, NORTHERN IRELAND, where the Irish exempted-development regime does NOT apply; Northern Ireland has its own permitted development rules. The Republic of Ireland figures below apply only to a buyer siting the building in the Republic: 30 m2 back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), combined across structures, behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Atlas holds no verified floor area for this product. A 'Lodge' marketed for overnight use would in any case fail the no-habitation condition and would need either permission or the new Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, 14 days' notice, expires 31 December 2030). Homeowner implication: confirm both the floor area AND which jurisdiction's rules apply to your site before assuming any exemption. AUDIT NOTE: approved-vocabulary wording normalised at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit; classification unchanged.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Berko is Northern Ireland based (Dungiven, Co. Derry), where the Irish regime does not apply. For a Republic site: 30 m2 back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), combined across structures, behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Atlas holds no verified floor area. A shepherd's hut used for sleeping fails the no-habitation condition. Homeowner implication: confirm floor area, intended use and applicable jurisdiction before assuming exemption. AUDIT NOTE: approved-vocabulary wording normalised at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit; classification unchanged.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No area, no dimensions and no product URL are held; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and makes the structural point plainly: a BESPOKE product has no fixed size by definition, so a measurement can exist only at as-quoted level and never at product level. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be run against this record and must be run against the as-ordered dimensions. THAT IS NOT A DOCUMENTATION GAP BUT A PROPERTY OF THE PRODUCT, and it has a useful consequence for the buyer: because the size is chosen rather than fixed, the planning outcome is chosen too. A bespoke room can be specified deliberately to sit inside the combined 30 m2 once every existing structure in the garden has been counted, and that is a conversation to have with the designer at the outset rather than a constraint discovered afterwards. Conditions applying whatever is specified: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure your existing garden structures FIRST, subtract from 30 m2, and give the designer the remaining figure as the external footprint budget.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. 'DELUXE' IS A SPECIFICATION LABEL, NOT A SIZE. A SECOND QUESTION SITS BEHIND THE AREA ONE: a TREATMENT ROOM implies clients visiting the property, which raises a CHANGE-OF-USE question distinct from the exemption's area test. Commercial use is not incidental use, and nothing has been assumed about how the buyer intends to run it. SUPPLIER STATUS — BIG MAN TINY HOMES, 4 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). All 4 REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: no area is published for any of the four, and not one model name carries a dimension — every name describes FIT-OUT or USE instead: with storage, with bathroom and kitchenette, multi use, deluxe treatment room. That is an unusual catalogue pattern and it is diagnostic: this supplier sells configurations, not sizes. WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE MISSING NUMBERS: on two of the four products the fit-out itself is the planning issue. The bathroom-and-kitchenette unit is equipped for habitation and would fall outside Class 3 on use whatever its area; the treatment room raises change of use. Obtaining the areas would resolve only half this range. SUPPLIER OMISSION, recorded once: no dimensions, no floor areas and no height data are published for any product. AVAILABILITY CONTEXT from the certified AM-005 layer: an Irish manufacturer at Bandon, Co. Cork, building complete units and craning them on site — so these are genuinely purchasable in the Republic and the planning position matters in practice. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: ask for a dimensioned drawing AND state your intended use; on this range the second question is the harder one.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE FIT-OUT DECIDES THIS PRODUCT: a unit with BOTH a bathroom AND a kitchenette is equipped for habitation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION. Regardless of its area, this product is unlikely to qualify as an exempt garden structure. THE APPLICABLE ROUTE WOULD BE CLASS 3A: detached auxiliary dwelling, 32-45 m2, to the rear, linked to the services of the principal house, on 14 days' notice to the planning authority, expiring 31 December 2030. That route CANNOT BE TESTED without an area — and it has a 32 m2 FLOOR, so a smaller unit falls between the two routes and needs full permission. Nothing inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a consent question before it is a size question. Take planning advice before ordering.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m height for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds NO area, NO dimensions and no derivable footprint; nothing estimated. THE INTEGRAL STORAGE COUNTS: storage built into the unit falls inside the same combined allowance, so the figure needed is the TOTAL external footprint, not the office section alone. SUPPLIER OMISSION, recorded: the product name describes fit-out and carries no dimension. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the total external footprint in square metres, office and store together, before assuming exemption.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. 'MULTI USE' DESCRIBES FLEXIBILITY, NOT A SIZE, and has not been treated as a measurement — but it does raise the use condition, because the exemption holds only while the building stays incidental to the house and is not slept in. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in writing, and be specific about which of the multiple uses you actually intend.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer records that the Lasita product page for the Brava returned METADATA ONLY, with no specification table, on two separate attempts — while every other Lasita page returned a full table first time. The model may be withdrawn or the page broken. No area is held and nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — LASITA MAJA, 10 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. Five sit within the exemption on floor area (Sacramento 8.2, Miami 2.0 8.2, Carroz 15.96, New York 20.40 external, New Orleans 23.43 external), FOUR are over the exemption limit (Falkland 33.06, Hawaii 40.56, Orinoco 37.50, Domeo 10 38.25 m2 external) and one requires product-specific verification. All Tier A. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Lasita is one of the best-disclosing manufacturers in the catalogue — external wall dimensions and internal floor size that reconcile to the centimetre — and it still produces the highest failure rate on the planning test of any supplier so far, four of nine measured products. THE REASON IS THE GAP BETWEEN FLOOR AND ENVELOPE: on the Domeo 10 and Orinoco the internal floor is barely half the external envelope, so a buyer reading the floor figure would assume comfortable exemption on a building that is not exempt at all. Good disclosure does not protect a homeowner who reads the wrong number. HEIGHT IS A SECOND SYSTEMATIC TRAP: Lasita roofs are SHINGLED, not tiled or slated, so the 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m across the range. TWO PRODUCTS ALSO FAIL ON HEIGHT and one, the Orinoco, carries a supplier data defect that makes its height unverifiable. CATEGORY, restated once from AM-001: only the New York is listed by the manufacturer for workshop and office use; the rest are garages, storage buildings or outdoor-living models miscategorised here as Garden Rooms. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: use the EXTERNAL envelope for the planning test, never the floor size. AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. The '44' in the name is WALL THICKNESS IN MILLIMETRES, not a floor area — a common misreading. No audited area held. Homeowner implication: ask ABC Gardenhouse IRL Ltd for the external footprint in m2.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 by S.I. 338 of 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, AND IT IS TO THE SUPPLIER'S CREDIT: THIS SUPPLIER PUBLISHES NO INCORRECT IRISH PLANNING CLAIM. Its FAQ states only that 'in most cases, garden rooms don't require planning permission as long as they fall within certain height and size restrictions' and then directs the reader to 'check local regulations or consult with us for advice'. It names no threshold, no height figure and no jurisdiction. THAT IS THE CORRECT POSITION FOR A CROSS-BORDER SUPPLIER and it is rarer in this catalogue than it should be: Luxury Garden Studios publishes a claim that conflates the 30 m2 incidental route with the separate 32–45 m2 Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route; Cabin Master and Booths Garden Studios publish UK permitted-development and Caravan Act positions that do not apply in Ireland at all. A supplier trading on both sides of the border faces two different regimes, and declining to state a single figure is the honest answer. THE STRUCTURAL POINT FOR THIS SUPPLIER: because every build is bespoke, THE HOMEOWNER CONTROLS THE PLANNING OUTCOME. Unlike a fixed-model supplier where the area is given and the buyer must accept it, here the footprint is specified at design stage — so the exemption can be designed for deliberately. That is a genuine advantage, available only to a buyer who knows the conditions before the design meeting. USE VARIES ACROSS THE RANGE: the Home Office and Sensory Room sit most comfortably within incidental use; Extra Living Space is compatible provided it is not slept in; the Salon/Studio raises a change-of-use question because clients visit the property. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: arrive at the design meeting knowing the 30 m2 combined allowance, the 3 m / 4 m height limits and the incidental-use and no-habitation conditions, and have the room designed to fit them. ATLAS MAKES NO PLANNING DETERMINATION on any product in this range.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. On a Republic of Ireland site the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 by S.I. 338 of 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space retained, 3 m height for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, and NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds NO area and NO dimensions for this product, because it is bespoke; nothing estimated. The area test cannot be run until a design is agreed. THE USE CONDITION IS THE LIVE ONE ON THIS PRODUCT: 'Extra Living Space' is published for 'relaxing, entertaining, or giving your family more room to live'. Day use incidental to the house is compatible with the exemption; SLEEPING IN IT IS NOT, whatever the area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle the footprint on a dimensioned drawing at design stage, and be clear with the planning authority that the room will not be slept in.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area, no dimensions and no internal height; nothing estimated. HEIGHT IS A DOUBLE CONSTRAINT ON A GYM AND BOTH SIDES ARE UNRESOLVED: the exemption caps EXTERNAL height at 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, while overhead training needs INTERNAL clear height — and the supplier publishes neither figure. A flat-roofed gym designed for overhead pressing has to fit the internal requirement inside a 3 m external envelope, which is achievable but must be designed for deliberately, not assumed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bring the equipment list and the height requirement to the design meeting, and get both external and internal heights onto the drawing.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE FAVOURABLE POINT FOR THIS USE: a home office used by the occupants of the house is the clearest example of incidental use there is, so of the six styles in this range it is the one least likely to trouble the use condition. Area remains the open question. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: because the building is bespoke you control the footprint — specify it under 30 m2 combined with anything already in the garden and the exemption is within reach on area. Get the figure on a drawing first.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND A CHANGE-OF-USE QUESTION SITS BEHIND IT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE HARDER QUESTION IS USE, NOT SIZE: this product is published explicitly for running a business from home — 'Ideal for beauty, hair, therapy, or creative studios' with 'a welcoming environment for clients'. CLIENTS VISITING THE PROPERTY IS NOT INCIDENTAL USE, and commercial operation raises a change-of-use question distinct from the exemption's area test. Nothing has been assumed about how the buyer intends to run it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: take planning advice on the intended commercial use BEFORE ordering. On this product the consent question comes before the size question.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. USE POSITION: a sensory room used by members of the household for relaxation and regulation is incidental use, and sits comfortably inside the exemption's use test — sleeping in it does not. Area remains the open question and is set at design stage. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the room is being provided to meet a specific need, raise that with the planning authority early rather than late; the area and height conditions still apply in full, and clarity ahead of the build is worth more than a retrospective argument.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No area, no dimensions and no product URL are held; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and classifies this as a RANGE-LEVEL record that must be split into its constituent models before any measurement can attach. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. Conditions applying to whichever model is built: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: identify the specific CUBE model and obtain its external footprint and overall height in writing before drawing any planning conclusion. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes the organisation 'Garden Rooms' for the Planning Considerations layer — 3 Garden Room records, ALL classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, and all three NON-SPECIFIC BY CONSTRUCTION rather than through supplier omission: the Bespoke Garden Room has no fixed size by definition, this CUBE Garden Room Range is a range, and the Ultimate Garden Room Range is a range that the certified AM-001 layer additionally records as having no organisation link at all. Not one holds a dimension or a URL, and not one identifies a single building against which the 30 m2 test could be run. RECORD DEFECTS recorded once, not corrected, architecture frozen: this organisation's name, 'Garden Rooms', is also the Atlas Product Category name, which makes supplier attribution ambiguous in any listing showing category and supplier side by side; and the certified AM-001 supplier status records TWO products for this organisation while the Products table now shows three, the third being the Ultimate Garden Room Range. Both should be reconciled at the Layer Completion Audit. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 12 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: internal versus external not stated; nothing deducted. WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026. This classification is driven by the EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT, which is the measure the exemption uses, and the distinction is decisive on this product. Yardbox publishes both: Footprint 6.2 m × 4.2 m = 26.04 m2; Living Space 24 m2. Both recorded exactly as published; nothing estimated or converted. On the internal 24 m2 figure it would have looked compliant under the old rule — which is exactly the error a homeowner makes when they check the living-space number against the allowance. HEADROOM IS THIN AND THE HEIGHT HAS NONE: about 3.96 m2 of the combined allowance remains for every other structure, so a plot with any existing shed or garage will very likely exceed the limit once this is added. Published height is 2.5-3 m, which sits AT the 3 m ceiling for a non-pitched roof with no margin — the height condition should be confirmed for the exact specification quoted, because a raised base or a thicker floor build-up could push it over. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. WHY THIS PRODUCT IS DIRECTLY CONSEQUENTIAL: Yardbox is Co. Down based and states it serves both Ireland and Northern Ireland, so this is an Irish-reachable product sitting close to two limits at once. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: total every existing structure in the garden, and get the finished height above ground level confirmed in writing before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Yardbox for the Planning Considerations layer — 3 Garden Room products: The Whistler at a 10.24 m2 footprint and The Vancouver at 16.64 m2, both sitting within the exemption on floor area, and this Toronto at 26.04 m2, within it only because of the 27 July 2026 increase. THIS IS THE BEST-DOCUMENTED SUPPLIER IN THE LAYER FOR PLANNING PURPOSES: Yardbox is only the second supplier in the entire Garden Room catalogue, after Sanctum, to publish usable internal area separately from footprint, the first to publish both side by side, and it publishes heights as well — so all three products can be tested on both statutory criteria from the supplier's own material, which is true of almost nothing else in this layer. THE ONE CAUTION THAT APPLIES ACROSS THE RANGE: the marketing copy on every model quotes the INTERNAL dimension as though it were the size of the building, so the very disclosure that makes these products testable is also the thing a casual reader will get wrong. CROSS-LAYER INTEGRITY ISSUE recorded once, without altering certified data: the same supplier comparison table lists the Bothan modular home at a 10 m × 4 m footprint, 40 m2, but 45 m2 of living space — an internal area larger than its own footprint, which cannot be right. The Bothan is a Home rather than a Garden Room and is out of scope here, but Yardbox markets it against the 32-45 m2 Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling band where the exact area is decisive, so the contradiction should be resolved with the supplier before any Bothan figure is relied on. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. A SEPARATE AND DECISIVE POINT ON USE: the product name states the intended use — glamping accommodation. That is commercial hospitality and overnight habitation, neither of which is use incidental to the enjoyment of a house, so this product falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption on USE alone, at any floor area. Commercial letting in a domestic back garden is a change of use that normally requires planning permission in its own right, independently of the size of the building. VOCABULARY LIMITATION recorded once for this layer: the approved classification set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use, so the closest approved value is retained and the use exclusion is stated here in full. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not treat this as a garden room. If the intention is short-term letting, the planning question is about change of use rather than about 30 m2, and it should be put to your local authority planning office before any purchase.
